7-day annualised return*: XX%
1-day annualised return*: XX%#
30-day annualised return*: XX%
Most recent 1-year return*: XX%
*Computation basis and periods covered:
#For the most up-to-date daily figure, please refer to [www.xxx.com].
judgments.explanation: The pixels show four return-summary columns in the left-to-right order transcribed here. Each has an asterisk after “return”; the 1-day value additionally has a superscript # after “XX%”. The # refers to the daily-figure footnote, while the asterisks refer to the computation-basis text. The inserted return labels and percentage placeholders are printed content, so their omission is not merely typographic. The supplied right token “XX%*” also changes the printed # to an asterisk. Superscript positioning alone would be typographic, but substituting a different footnote symbol changes text and its reference. The displayed token intervals do not establish how either complete extraction associates all four columns.
judgments.affected_condition: The association of each return period with its percentage placeholder and the computation-basis and daily-update footnotes.

Splitting that compound into the extraction tokens “1” and “-year” preserves its characters, order and duration; the listed replacement is a tokenization difference. The other supplied location points to the numeral in “Illustrative example 1”, which is separate from the affected compound and does not establish an additional change.

judgments.explanation: The note visibly ends its parenthetical calculation description with “reinvested)]”: a closing parenthesis followed by a closing square bracket. Both extraction variants preserve these characters in the same order. Separating the final square bracket into its own token is typographic and does not omit or change wording.
judgments.affected_condition: The closing punctuation of the calculation description preceding the historical returns.

The supplied locations also include unrelated occurrences of “of” and “5” in the body; matching those common tokens does not establish that those body passages are part of this insertion. This judgment concerns the visible footer wording, not its legal applicability.
